findings.passage: “The SAVE Act proposed by House Republicans is a terrible piece of legislation. It doesn’t secure our elections; it adds unnecessary barriers that would prevent people from exercising their right to participate in the democratic process,” said Congressman Gabe Amo.
findings.note: Official statement issued the day he voted against the SAVE Act (H.R. 22). The same release says existing law already bans noncitizens from voting in federal elections and names veterans abroad, married women who changed names, and people without a passport as groups it would burden.

findings.passage: I strongly oppose this legislation. We will not restore trust in our elections through misguided efforts to exclude eligible American voters. Let’s get back to the business of carrying out America’s values by investing in voter registration and making sure every American can make their voice heard.”
findings.note: Closing lines of the same statement, in his words.

findings.passage: Democratic Congressman Gabe Amo said in a statement of his own that noncitizens already “cannot vote in federal elections,” and that the bill “is just fearmongering.”
findings.note: WPRI (a Rhode Island TV station) quoting his statement the day after the House passed the 2024 SAVE Act (H.R. 8281). The reporter's sentence is given whole; only the quoted pieces are his words. The article also quotes him saying the bill affects "52% of citizens who do not have a passport by adding red tape and requiring original documents they may not have."
